llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent and purpose-aligned, but it asks users to pass a powerful SocialEcho Team API key on the command line for tools that can publish content and sync TikTok Shop products.

dimensions.detail: Network requests are restricted in code to the SocialEcho production or development HTTPS hosts, and the skill tells agents not to search local files, environment variables, credential stores, or shell history for keys.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package has no dependencies and no install-time scripts; it exposes local Node.js CLI entry points only.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Live writes are documented and gated with dry-run, --execute, and matching --confirm-account-id, but the required Team API key is documented as --api-key, which can expose a bearer credential through shell history, process listings, or logs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence or privilege escalation was found, but the command-line credential flow is under-protected for a key that may authorize account reads, public publishing, and product synchronization.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the bundled CLI helpers: read SocialEcho team/account/content data, prepare uploads, query platform resources, and perform explicit live writes for article publishing and TikTok Shop product sync.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only with a least-privilege SocialEcho Team API key, avoid putting real keys directly in shell commands or shared scripts, rotate any key that may have been logged, and require a fresh user confirmation before any publish or TikTok Shop sync action.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The description-behavior mismatch concern was not supported when reviewing the whole artifact: the package includes the documented team, account, article, report, upload, Reddit, Pinterest, TikTok Shop, music, publish, and sync helpers.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The default language is zh_CN in the client and OpenAPI specs, while English is also supported. This is disclosed and user-overridable, so it is a usability/policy note rather than the main security concern.
[T09] unexpected: The credential concern is supported: the skill requires a Team API key via --api-key, and that transport is not necessary to the purpose and can leak through ordinary command-line handling.
